core_obligations: Define the map in one direction (proof lines 1646-1654): send a locally closed subspace Z of X to the locally closed subscheme Z' = Z x_X U of U; it is immediate from the definition that Z' -> U is an immersion, closed, or open whenever Z -> X is, and that Z' is invariant under the relation.

Construct the inverse (proof lines 1656-1676): given an invariant immersion Z' -> U, let R' be the restriction of the relation to Z'; since R' is exhibited as a fibre product over the source and target maps it is again an etale equivalence relation on Z', so Z = Z'/R' is an algebraic space with U x_X Z = Z'; the property of being an immersion is preserved under base change and is fppf local on the base, and since immersions are separated and locally quasi-finite they descend along fppf coverings.

Conclude (proof lines 1676-1679): the descent criterion applies to the surjective etale morphism U -> X and the property immersion, so Z -> X is representable and an immersion, that is a subspace; the two constructions are clearly inverse to each other.
proof_roadmap: Send a locally closed subspace to its base change along the presentation and note the invariance.
Given an invariant immersion, restrict the relation and use the presentation theorem to build the subspace.
Apply fppf descent of immersions to identify the result with a subspace of X.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for the algebraic space X presented by an etale equivalence relation R on a scheme U there is a canonical bijection between the R-invariant locally closed subschemes of U and the locally closed subspaces of X, matching closedness and openness (statement lines 1631-1644). The proof (proof lines 1646-1681) sends a subspace to its base change along the presentation, constructs the inverse by restricting the relation to an invariant subscheme and applying the presentation theorem, and uses fppf descent of immersions to conclude. H2: two constructions with a descent step, written out in full.
